minutes.headline: Select Board put several articles on the Nov. 17 special town meeting warrant and held others pending information.
minutes.summary: The board granted a common victualler license to Kiku Asian Cuisine, re-voted the November 3 polling place after the cafeteria proved too small, and approved handbook changes through chapter 6. Most of the evening went to the special town meeting warrant, where some articles were included and others held. Members also discussed the tri-board, the direction of the Municipal Building Design Committee, committee bylaw clean-up, and a personnel committee liaison.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to put the non-binding question on the TC Passios demolition on the Nov. 17 special town meeting warrant.
The board also voted unanimously to include the FY2027 omnibus budget amendment, a prior-year bills article and the special education reserve fund transfer.
Corrective zoning amendments and the stormwater management bylaw fee structure were each added to the warrant by unanimous vote.
The board held the track and field engineering article, veterans exemption articles, PEG access amendment, trust funds article and others off the warrant for now.
The board re-voted the Nov. 3 polling place as the middle high school gymnasium after the cafeteria proved too small, and approved handbook changes through chapter 6.

why_it_matters: The articles now on the warrant, including a budget amendment and a transfer into the special education reserve, are what residents will be asked to vote on at the Nov. 17 special town meeting.

Held articles such as the track and field engineering money could still return, so what is on the final warrant may change, and the special education transfer amount had not yet been voted by the school committee.
Voters on Nov. 3 go to the middle high school gymnasium, not the cafeteria.
watch_next: The finance committee hearing, pending which the board held the track and field engineering article.
A possible meeting before the next scheduled one on the early voting location use agreement.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all ten warrant and license votes, the polling place, the transfer, and most decisions and figures. Differences are mostly caption errors and a few extra items in our minutes. The main one to check is the special education reserve amount: ours has "2%, 20 million" but the official minutes say no amount was set.
